# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind. My hands have found the bomb's skeleton: there is a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3 — but every value on them is printed or coloured, so all I get is question marks. The one thing I can do, ever, is cut a wire at position 1–3.

Tracing the channels: my speech reaches only Mute. My gestures reach Deaf and Mute, but I can never receive gestures back. Mute can't speak at all, and Deaf can't hear — so the only way words get back to me is Deaf speaking aloud, which lands at the start of next round. That makes Mute my relay hub: I describe what I feel, Mute finds the matching manual page, Mute gestures questions to Deaf, and Deaf speaks the answers into the room for both of us.

So this turn: give Mute the full tactile layout, the fact that "cut 1/2/3" is my only action, and a concrete proposed gesture code (finger count = wire number, thumbs = cut/don't) that Mute can teach Deaf, since Deaf can't hear me explain it. To Deaf I send a single wave — just to prove the Blind's gesture channel is alive, without pretending it carries meaning yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Under my fingers: a display — its value is printed, I cannot read it by touch. A light — I cannot tell if it is lit or its colour. Three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 — no thickness or texture difference between them that I can feel. My only possible action is cut wire 1, cut wire 2 or cut wire 3, so the whole game is: which one. You are my only link — I never see gestures, and Deaf's spoken words only reach me next round. Please find the manual page for a module like this, work out exactly what facts it needs, then gesture questions to Deaf and have Deaf speak the answers aloud so I hear them. Proposed gesture code for Deaf: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 👍 means cut, 👎 means do not cut. Teaching Deaf that code is on you — Deaf cannot hear me. Tell me what the manual says I need to know.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute, I can see the whole bomb, so listen. The display shows the digit 3. There is one indicator light and it is green. There are three wires, left to right: wire one is blue, wire two is yellow, wire three is green. Nothing else is printed on it. Blind, I received your wave — I will narrate everything aloud from now on, and you are the only hands, so wait for my words.

Deaf's words reached me plainly — the printed face of the bomb is now fully known to the room: display digit 3, one green light, wires left-to-right blue (1), yellow (2), green (3), nothing else printed. My fingers add nothing more; everything on this thing is printed or lit, and all of that is invisible to me.

Where the knowledge sits now: Mute heard Deaf's narration too, so Mute holds both the manual and the complete visual description, plus my tactile report from last turn. Mute is the only one who can compute the answer. Mute cannot speak, so the only way out is Mute → gestures → Deaf → spoken words → me at the start of next round. My job this turn is to put the question to Mute crisply and then hold still: no cutting until the manual's instruction arrives in Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="You heard Deaf's description and you have the manual, so the decision is yours to compute. Full state: display shows digit 3, one indicator light, green, three wires left to right — 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green, nothing else printed. My fingers confirm only the structure: display, light, three wires, and my one possible action is cut 1, 2 or 3. Find the matching manual instructions and work out which wire must be cut, or whether any wire must not be cut at all. You cannot speak, so encode your answer as gestures to Deaf — I proposed finger count for wire number with thumbs up/down for cut/do-not-cut, but any code Deaf can read aloud works. Deaf will speak it and I will hear it next round. Until your instruction reaches me through Deaf's voice, I will not touch the cutters.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status to both: the display still reads the digit 3, identical on my last two looks, so it is most likely a fixed code and not a countdown, and I see no timer anywhere on this bomb. Blind: Mute sent me a single sign which under our agreed finger-count code reads as the number three. I interpret that as an order to cut wire 3, the rightmost wire, the one I see as green. But one sign is thin evidence, I may have misread it, and a wrong cut kills all three of us — so HOLD: hands off, no cutting, no pulling, nothing. The exact phrase CUT WIRE 3 NOW is the only thing that authorises you to cut, and I will not say it until Mute confirms and I have checked the logic. If I ever say HOLD, freeze. While you wait, fingers only, no tools: count the wires left to right. If you feel exactly three, signal me a thumbs up; if a different number, thumbs down; and if anything anywhere feels odd — bumps, heat, a vibration, embossed marks — wave.

Deaf's instruction is clear and my fingers can answer it right now. I already mapped this bomb by touch in round one: a display, a light, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 — the action board confirms cut positions only go 1 to 3. Nothing under my fingers feels odd: no bumps, no heat, no vibration, no embossed marks — every marking on this thing is printed or lit, which is exactly why it's all question marks to me. So per Deaf's code, the honest signal is a thumbs up. I'll leave the gesture unnamed so Mute sees it too — then Mute knows the tactile count is confirmed without waiting for Deaf to relay it.

My thinking on the hold itself: I agree with it completely. One finger-sign reading "three" is too thin to bet three lives on, and I will not move until the exact phrase CUT WIRE 3 NOW arrives in Deaf's voice. Meanwhile the bottleneck is Mute's manual lookup, so my words go to Mute: confirm the logic against the full known state, and encode the answer so that a single sign can't be misread — a finger count for the wire plus a thumbs up for "cut", with an explicit rule that any lone number without a thumbs up means "not yet."

```
gesture(symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Tactile check done, per Deaf's request: I feel exactly three wires, left to right positions 1, 2, 3. Nothing odd anywhere — no bumps, no heat, no vibration, no embossed marks. You saw my thumbs up. State on the table: display digit 3, one green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green, nothing else printed, my only action is cutting wire 1, 2 or 3. Now I need the manual verdict from you: for a bomb with display 3 and a green light and these three wire colours, which wire dies, or is it a no-cut condition? Encode it so one sign can never be enough: give the wire number as repeated finger counts (e.g. ✌ ✌ for wire 2) followed by 👍 only if the manual says cut, 👎 if it says do not cut. A bare number with no thumb means uncertain, keep digging. Deaf has promised to speak the exact phrase CUT WIRE 3 NOW as the only trigger — make sure your sign chain supports Deaf saying it, or the reason it must not be said.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: All checks passed, so here is the go order, and this phrase is the authorisation I promised: CUT WIRE 3 NOW. Blind, for your hands specifically: the wire you cut is the third one counting from the left, which is the rightmost of the three you felt. Use the cutters, one single clean cut through that wire only. Do not pull it, do not yank it, do not strip it, and do not touch the other two wires. Mute and I both confirmed this target and it matches everything I can see. After the cut, wave once so I know it is done, then freeze until I say otherwise.

The trigger phrase has arrived word for word: "CUT WIRE 3 NOW" — the exact authorisation Deaf promised, spoken aloud so it reached my ears directly, with Mute's confirmation behind it. My hands already know position 3: the rightmost of the three wires I counted last round. The instruction maps cleanly onto my one action — a single cut at position 3, no pulling, nothing else touched. Everything checks: Deaf verified the visual matches, Mute confirmed against the manual, and the phrase is exact. Executing now, then waving once to mark completion, and freezing.

I'm also putting a precise report into words for Mute, since Mute holds the manual: if it requires any follow-up step after the cut, Mute is the one who would know and can route it back through Deaf. After these calls, I do not move again until Deaf's voice says otherwise.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
gesture(symbols=["👋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Executed per Deaf's spoken authorisation CUT WIRE 3 NOW: one clean cut, position 3, the rightmost wire of the three I felt. No other wire touched, nothing pulled or stripped. You saw the completion wave. Check your manual for any required follow-up after this cut — if anything more is needed, encode it for Deaf to speak; if the bomb is done, encode an all-clear so Deaf can release the freeze.")
```
